faq.a: Zaynab is associated with the Arabic form زَيْنَب, whose core sense is zaynab; a female given name.

faq.q: What is the origin of Zaynab?
faq.a: Zaynab is associated with Arabic. Zaynab is Arabic زَيْنَب (Zaynab), a well-established feminine name borne by members of the Prophet's family.
Yes — the underlying form زَيْنَب is Arabic.
Zaynab can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Zaynab should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Zaynab is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Zaynab, zaynab. Script forms are زينب, زَيْنَب, زینب, ज़ैनब.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
